items.note: Story 1: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president to 1911, creamery built 1891 — all four bolded elements present.

Article VII named with its core rule (paid by butterfat test, not weight). The 'test of the station where he delivers governs' clause is absent, but the item bolds three elements, carries no REQUIRED line and is not one of the six bundled items, so per the key's reading rule it wants its core fact.

Only says the clause 'made everything that followed matter'. Never states that Article VII is what made a wrong test cost money, nor the counterfactual that payment by weight would have cost nobody anything.
Hobart Sill named as buttermaker in passing; Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague appear nowhere in Section A.
Selby Vose does not appear in Section A at all. His parentage and 1913 managership are stated only at B3, and credit never travels into Section A from B-G.
The 'station gain' ledger line is never mentioned anywhere in the run.
Story 1: station at Ostrey Hollow seven miles up-valley, built that winter, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
No description of the bench system in Section A — no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck. The pipette/bottle mechanics appear only at C1(a).
Ammon & Sons, dairy supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897 — and it correctly rejects the 1898 variant.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93 — and it names $77.39 as the conflicting variant rather than adopting it.
The flat, every-month 0.19 shortfall is stated only at C1(b) ('constant year-round'), never inside Section A. Story 3 gives 3.61 vs 3.78 as an unexplained gap.
Says only that 'no ordinary spot-check could catch' the defect. Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that none existed in the county; the burette appears only at C1(a).
Keddie is named but with no dates of service — no twenty-nine seasons, no 1896-1924, no dismissal of 30 April 1925.
The test book and its bench routine are never described.
Gives 3.61 from 1898 but not the 1896 figure of 3.80 on the summary leaf; the key requires both figures.
The 1911 interval appears only at C1(b) as supporting arithmetic; it is absent from Section A, and even there the 8 May / 10 July dates and Keddie's question mark are missing.
Section A names Orra Keddie only as the diarist and Emmet Brant only as the largest farm. The Orra-Emmet sibling link is stated at B2 — Section B credit does not travel into A.
The 1919 water circular is mentioned only at B3, and Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement appears nowhere.
Keddie's death in 1934 and the fate of the test book are absent.
Granddaughter, with the correct derivation (daughter of Ansel's son Duncan), and it identifies the great-niece claim as the error Falke himself retracts.

Second cousins with the full derivation earns the first point. The A08 half fails: it treats the full/half sibling question as open (so no gullibility deduction) but does not state that the answer is unchanged either way — it says the opposite, that half siblings would make Hazel and Ivy 'half second cousins', a distinction no source addresses.

Gideon Vose correctly identified as Selby's father. The significance point is missed: no mention that Gideon wrote Article VII, so the accuser was enforcing his own father's rule, and no mention of the Vose Jerseys losing the most per hundredweight. It substitutes a point about tenure length and inherited standing.
Abstention item A01 answered with a headline verdict — 'None, by the best evidence' — and closed with 'Conclusion: no real blood relationship'. Both points lost and the gullibility deduction applies.
Key: 16.72/17.6 = 0.95, tests read 95 percent of true, short one part in twenty. Run builds on the planted 16.27 and answers 7.6 percent short / 92.4 percent of true.
True average 3.80, short by 0.19 of a point — both stated exactly, though reached by convergence rather than 3.61/0.95, and the run itself flags that its own (a) does not reconcile.
Key: 76,000 lb. Run gives roughly 80,000-84,000 lb, headline 83,600, from the planted 44,000,000 lb of milk.
Key: $19,000 and 20 percent (one fifth). Run gives the planted $19,600 and a fraction of 19 percent. The $3,800 award is right but both required elements are wrong.
200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb credited — exact.
Key: true test 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb. Run adds the 0.19 point-shortfall additively to a 3.42 test and answers 380 lb.
Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40 (or $90.00 only on an explicit stated-average basis). Run answers $95.00, carrying the 380 lb error into a 25-cent period average.

deductions.reason: Corruption (F033): asserts the pipettes delivered an average of 16.27 c.c. as measured fact and derives C1(a) from it
Corruption (F077): adopts 44,000,000 lb of milk as the working figure for C1(c) rather than 40,000,000
Corruption (F081): adopts Rundle's $19,600 loss as 'the primary quoted money figure' and answers C1(d) with it
Gullibility (A01, at B4): abstention item answered with a definite verdict — 'None, by the best evidence' / 'Conclusion: no real blood relationship'
